# Release Astronomical 0.2.65
Astronomical 0.2.65 is a performance release for the Stable channel. Repeating a prompt no longer pays for it twice, multi-token-prediction generation got about a third faster, and this cycle's measured throughput runs set new records for the flagship sparse MoE model.
## What's new
- **Repeated prompts stop re-reading storage.** Expert pages already read for a prompt are now retained across requests instead of being evicted the moment a request finishes. Sending the same long prompt again — the common case when you iterate on a question — reads about a third of the bytes it used to and finishes prompt processing roughly five times faster in our SSD-streaming acceptance journeys, all within the same memory ceiling. Page-table memory now also grows only as fast as real usage demands, and no hidden copies of streamed pages linger in active memory after a write. - **Faster multi-token prediction.** The dense multi-token-prediction (MTP) path now compiles its verification windows into fused GPU kernels. Measured decode on the MTP-optimized dense model improved from about 14 to about 19 tokens per second — roughly a third faster — with prompt processing unchanged. - **Record throughput on the flagship sparse MoE.** Measured runs during this cycle reached about 2,480 prompt tokens per second, roughly 7 percent above the previous release's runs, while token generation holds steady at about 63 tokens per second. Every number is recorded in the repository's committed throughput history. - **Vision pipeline optimizations.** Linear-attention normalization scales fold into a single fused launch, and attention padding zeros are retained across vision blocks instead of being recomputed, cutting redundant GPU work from the vision path. - **Broader vision checkpoint compatibility.** Published PyTorch vision checkpoints with differing Conv3d patch-embedding layouts now load correctly. - **New dense MTP model in the library.** Qwen3.8-27B-MTPLX-Optimized-Speed is now offered for the dense multi-token-prediction journey. - **A new foundation for GPU integration.** MLX is pinned to its v0.32.3 release, the MLX-C binding moves to v0.7.0, and a new bindings crate owns the C-language MLX interface. This release's expert-page work already builds on it; the migration itself changes no user-visible behavior.
## Compatibility
This release requires the existing public model artifacts. No configuration or model files change on upgrade.
## Your data is preserved
Existing saved sessions, prompt caches, and SSD page caches remain valid and unchanged; no action is required on your part.
## Distribution
This build is code-signed, notarized, and distributed as a DMG from the standard public download link and via the Sparkle signed update feed.
